3. Location and Proximity
The project lies within the corporate limits of the city of Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. Harrisburg is the capital of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and the seat of Dauphin County. It is strategically located in the south central part of the state. This has contributed to the City's development as a transportation hub. The highway network for the area includes I-81, I-78, I-76, I-83, US 11, US 15, US 22, US 322 and US 422. The City is also served by two rail lines — the Reading and the Penn Central. Two airports serve the area — Olmstead State Airport (also known as Harrisburg International Airport), located 15 miles southeast of the City at Middletown, Pennsylvania, and the Harrisburg-York Airport located 4 miles due south of Harrisburg in York County, Pennsylvania.
The project itself is located in the westernmost part of the City along the east bank of the Susquehanna River. Since the City is irregular in shape, the project area, at midpoint, is located one mile northwest of the City's central business district (CBD) and the State Capitol Building (see Appendix B, Project Location Map, for this and other proximity measurements). The Governor's Mansion is located within the project area. There are six bridges immediately south of the project, intersecting Front Street, these bridges link the City to the western shore of the River.
Harrisburg has seven other areas in which Federally-assisted urban renewal activity is being either planned, being presently carried out or has been previously completed. They are as follows: (See appendix B Project Location Map).
a. The Hamilton Neighborhood Development Program (NDP)
(Project No. Pa. A-1) located 1 block due east of the subject project. NDP's conduct the same type of activities as conventional urban renewal projects; however, they are funded on an annual basis. The NDP Project is now in its third year of funding.
b. The Cameron-South Harrisburg Urban Renewal Project
(Pa. R-608(c)) which is now in the Survey and Planning stage of activity.
c. The Walnut Street Project
(Pa. R-302) nearing completion.
